text:
maria: Heads-up — we started seeing a weird pattern on eu2 around 10:08 UTC. Multiple tenants hit 95p token latency spikes for short bursts, had a thermal event on rack r24 around the same time. Possible tenant shadowing via KV cache churn.

infra-bot: alert: rack=r24 thermal_threshold=75C, avg_token_latency_up=23% (10:08:12 -> 10:09:05)

ashok: I can confirm. Stack traces show a lot of KV eviction churn and repeated cold-kv misses from one tenant (tenant-id: t-83c). That tenant saturated the warm-pool and caused prefetch storm.

zach: Seen similar impact earlier this month but less pronounced. Do we have heatmap vs tenant mappings for r24? link: https://telemetry.redwood/internal/eu2/r24/heatmap (private)

maria: I dumped a few logs, here's a snippet showing eviction loops and the scheduler reassigns:
```
2026-02-12T10:08:14Z evict: kv_cache t-83c victim=0x7fae size=120MB
2026-02-12T10:08:14Z prefetch: t-83c load=heavy -> warmpool_hit=low
2026-02-12T10:08:15Z sched: reassign pod p-992 -> rack r24
2026-02-12T10:08:16Z latency: token_p95=312ms -> baseline=256ms
```

tess: SLO impact? How many routes failed SLA windows during the window?

azch: (typo) zach: quick check: ~140 requests breached 200ms p95 in that minute, mostly chat endpoints. Not yet near page threshold but trending.

ryan: Any recent changes to warm-pool sizing or cache eviction policy for dedicated vs shared slices?

ashok: We rolled a cache eviction micro-tune yesterday on eu2 to reduce memory tailbloat, but default eviction aggressiveness increased 10%. That helps single-tenant memory but can amplify multi-tenant thrash when one tenant hits pathological access patterns.

maria: Proposal: temporary mitigation — 1) isolate t-83c by routing to a fractional dedicated slice (quiet-slice) 2) throttle its prefetch rate 3) back-off eviction aggressiveness on shared pools for eu2 until we patch detection. Thoughts?

ashok: +1 to isolation for immediate relief. We can flip routing via:
```
routerctl route set --tenant t-83c --target fractional-dedicated --children=2 --grace=30s
```
This will pin them to a small reserved slice and stop them thrashing shared warm-pools.

zach: Also recommend a short-term scheduler tweak: weight down prefetch for shared pools: `schedulerctl set prefetch_weight --pool shared --tenant-penalty 0.4`

ryan: If we move them to fractional-dedicated, cost goes up a bit. Estimate: ~0.6 GPU-hours extra for the hour. Worth it to protect other tenants.

tess: Can infra-bot post an automated follow-up in 30m with metric deltas after the route change? Want to confirm it actually lowers p95.

infra-bot: scheduled_check: will post delta metrics at +30m for rack=r24 and tenant=t-83c

maria: I'm going to run the route change now, will keep it as a transient mitigation.

ashok: Also adding a short-term detector to flag repeated eviction loops so we can auto-quarantine next time:
```
rule: eviction-loop-detect
if kv_evictions_per_min > 200 and repeat_count > 3 -> mark_quarantine(tenant)
actions: notify #eng-infra, throttle-prefetch, route-assign-fractional
```

zach: +1 to the detector. We should tune thresholds after the post-change telemetry.

maria: Done — routed t-83c to fractional-dedicated at 10:12:08 UTC.

infra-bot: action: route_change applied (tenant=t-83c -> fractional-dedicated slice s-401), timestamp=3890123468

ryan: Thumbs-up. If this repeats for other tenants we should scope a policy: auto-fallback when rack thermal + eviction loops coincide. Could save a lot of manual ops.

tess: Agreed. Also logging item: correlate thermal events and prefetch spikes in our anomaly dashboard — currently they're separate.

maria: I'll create a follow-up ticket to (1) persist detector, (2) add thermal+eviction correlation dashboard, (3) draft rollback plan for eviction micro-tune.

ashok: One more note — we should consider a temporary reduction of warm-pool share between shared tenants vs fractional_dedicated to limit blast radius.

zach: Putting a summary into #incidents after we confirm delta. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:

maria: Postmortem item if detector doesn't auto-fix. For now monitoring looks improved — infra-bot will confirm in 30m. :eyes:
